lesson.title: The e and the s
lesson.subtitle: Feminine -e wakes the sleeping final consonant (grand → grande); plural -s stays silent.

hook.title: The Consonant That Sleeps in the Masculine and Wakes in the Feminine
hook.content: Adding feminine -e wakes up the sleeping final consonant of the masculine adjective: grand (/ɡʁɑ̃/) → grande (/ɡʁɑ̃d/), petit (/pəti/) → petite (/pətit/), vert (/vɛʁ/) → verte (/vɛʁt/), content (/kɔ̃tɑ̃/) → contente (/kɔ̃tɑ̃t/), blanc (/blɑ̃/) → blanche (/blɑ̃ʃ/). Meanwhile, plural -s stays 100% silent!

footnotes.title: Four Written Forms, Only Two Spoken Sounds
footnotes.content: Across grand, grands, grande, grandes, singular and plural sound identical in each gender (/ɡʁɑ̃/ for masculine, /ɡʁɑ̃d/ for feminine)!

pattern.title: Feminine -e Wakes the Consonant; Plural -s Stays Silent
pattern.content: Match adjective endings to the noun's gender and number.
pattern.linguist_note: Plural -s in French nouns and adjectives is purely orthographic except in prevocalic liaison.
pattern.trap_note: Don't pronounce the final -s on plural adjectives like grands or petites!

exercises.prompt: Match each masculine adjective with its feminine twin:
exercises.target_answer: Elle est grande (/ɡʁɑ̃d/), Elle est petite (/pətit/), Elle est contente (/kɔ̃tɑ̃t/), La table est verte (/vɛʁt/), La maison est blanche (/blɑ̃ʃ/)
exercises.meaning: Il est grand (/ɡʁɑ̃/), Il est petit (/pəti/), Il est content (/kɔ̃tɑ̃/), Le jardin est vert (/vɛʁ/), Le mur est blanc (/blɑ̃/)
exercises.explanation: Feminine -e wakes the d, t, or turns -c into -che.

exercises.prompt: How many different pronunciations exist across the four written forms 'petit, petits, petite, petites'?
options: Two (/pəti/ for m.sg/pl, and /pətit/ for f.sg/pl)
exercises.target_answer: Two (/pəti/ for m.sg/pl, and /pətit/ for f.sg/pl)
exercises.meaning: Plural -s is silent, so singular and plural sound identical in each gender!
exercises.explanation: Only the feminine -e changes the pronunciation.

exercises.prompt: Write the feminine singular of 'blanc' ('white') to describe 'la maison':

exercises.idea: she is very happy and he is very tall
cues: She is very happy → Elle est très contente
and he is very tall → et il est très grand
idea_parts: feminine clause → Elle est très contente
masculine clause → et il est très grand
exercises.target_answer: Elle est très contente et il est très grand
exercises.meaning: She is very happy and he is very tall
exercises.explanation: Elle takes feminine contente; il takes masculine grand.

diagnosis.cue: Match contente to Elle and grand to il.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Les maisons blanches sont très grandes
exercises.target_answer: Les maisons blanches sont très grandes
exercises.meaning: The white houses are very big
exercises.explanation: Both blanches and grandes carry feminine -e plus plural -s.
exercises.affirmation: You wrote both feminine plural endings (-es) on blanches and grandes!

summary.outcome: Produce masculine, feminine, and plural adjective forms while keeping plural -s silent.

use_example.german: Les jardins sont verts et les maisons sont blanches.
use_example.english: The gardens are green and the houses are white.

summary.takeaway: Four written forms (grand, grands, grande, grandes), only two spoken sounds (/ɡʁɑ̃/ and /ɡʁɑ̃d/).
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([1102] Color & Size Gym): see how The e and the s leads directly into Color & Size Gym.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "She is very happy and he is very tall" in French:
twist.target_answer: Elle est très contente et il est très grand
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Elle est très contente et il est très grand" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of The e and the s.

grand.etymology_derivation: English 'grand' came straight from French; the feminine adds a silent -e, which wakes the silent d into sound: grand /ɡʁɑ̃/ → grande /ɡʁɑ̃d/.

petit.etymology_derivation: English 'petite' is the French feminine form, borrowed whole — the masculine is petit.

vert.etymology_derivation: Latin viridis → verdant, verdure — the green English kept in poetry.

blanc.etymology_derivation: Germanic blank 'shining white' → French blanc, English blank and blanket (the white cloth).

content.etymology_derivation: Latin contentus. Feminine wakes the silent t: contente /kɔ̃tɑ̃t/.

bon.etymology_derivation: Latin bonus 'good' — English borrowed the word back as 'bonus', a good thing added.

maison.etymology_derivation: Latin mansiō 'a staying' → maison and mansion: the house you stay in, and the big one.

jardin.etymology_derivation: Frankish *gardo gave English garden/yard and French jardin.
